Ecosystem corpora

The pinned repository sets and blind selection rules for each ecosystem detector. The summary and the accuracy table are on Validation.

Kubernetes corpus

Thirty-six public repositories at pinned commits cover the kubernetes detector. Targeted (chosen knowing their result): argoproj/argocd-example-apps (Helm and kustomize applications, including a Chart.yaml dependency on the retired Helm stable repository), kelseyhightower/ingress-with-static-ip, unixhot/salt-kubebin (a CronJob and three Ingresses), kubernetes/examples (two PodSecurityPolicy documents, plus the two end-of-life base images the container detector reports there), and lusyoe/springboot-k8s-example (a Helm template and a plain manifest). ahmetb/kubernetes-network-policy-recipes is a targeted zero-finding companion (modern NetworkPolicy examples only), added so the kubernetes corpus still has two empty expected lists after argocd-example-apps gained the Helm stable finding.

Blind (rule below): kelseyhightower/kubernetes-cluster-federation (extensions/v1beta1 Deployments, ReplicaSets, and an Ingress), motiv-labs/janus (a PodDisruptionBudget and an Ingress, plus Go and Action findings), FairwindsOps/pluto (two extensions/v1beta1 Deployments outside its test directories), luksa/kubernetes-in-action (thirty-odd manifests across extensions, apps/v1beta1 and v1beta2, PodSecurityPolicy, CronJob, StatefulSet, CRD, and Ingress), ossf/package-analysis (an autoscaling/v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler), knrt10/kubernetes-basicLearning (a networking.k8s.io/v1beta1 Ingress), and five with no Kubernetes finding: hasura/skor (the removed version appears only as a kind: List item), stefanprodan/gitops-istio (the removed version appears only as a Flagger autoscalerRef), doitintl/kube-no-trouble (the removed versions are in fixtures/), elastic/crd-ref-docs, and yaml-schema/yaml-schema, shepherd44/helm-charts (current API versions).

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the Kubernetes ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of these repositories has a migration commit for the finding, so none is cited. The rules' dates and removal releases come from the Kubernetes migration guide, not from these repositories. A run of npm run validate:public-repos -- --ecosystem kubernetes on 2026-10-23 over the seventeen Kubernetes entries reported no false positives or false negatives, with 67 expected kubernetes findings, all true.

Correction (blind ground truth). The FairwindsOps/pluto entry was missing one expected finding: e2e/tests/assets/list/list-deployment-deprecated-and-non-deprecated.yaml line 3, an extensions/v1beta1 Deployment inside a kind: List document. The first corpus run with the kind: List parser reported it as unexpected. A re-read of the pinned file confirmed it is a real removed API, so the expected list was extended after that run, and this paragraph records the change. The earlier count of 67 expected kubernetes findings predates this correction.

Kubernetes blind selection

The five earliest Kubernetes repositories were chosen knowing their result, so each records selection: "targeted"; the twelve below record selection: "blind".

The blind rule, fixed on 2026-10-23 before Offing ran on these additions: GitHub code search restricted to --extension yaml (gh search code <query> --limit 60) for each of extensions/v1beta1, policy/v1beta1, batch/v1beta1, autoscaling/v2beta2, and networking.k8s.io/v1beta1 (removed API groups, expected to produce findings), and apps/v1 Deployment (current API, expected to produce none). Per query, walk the results in order and keep the first two unique repositories, skipping forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus or chosen by an earlier query, and repositories larger than 5,000 KB on GitHub. Pin each at its default-branch commit on that date. The twelve are hasura/skor, kelseyhightower/kubernetes-cluster-federation, motiv-labs/janus, FairwindsOps/pluto, luksa/kubernetes-in-action, doitintl/kube-no-trouble, ossf/package-analysis, stefanprodan/gitops-istio, knrt10/kubernetes-basicLearning, elastic/crd-ref-docs, yaml-schema/yaml-schema, and shepherd44/helm-charts. The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list above, not a re-run, is the record.

Ground truth: for each repository every apiVersion line naming a removed group and version was listed with grep over the pinned YAML files and compared with the report, independently of Offing's own output, and each reported finding's kind was read from its manifest. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the kind.

Kubernetes stable expansion (2026-11-08)

To meet the stable evidence minimums of decision 0013 (at least 20 repositories with Kubernetes findings, 4 zero-finding Kubernetes-ecosystem repositories, at least two thirds blind, at least 60 kubernetes.* expected findings), the Kubernetes corpus gains further blind repositories. The selection rule below was fixed on 2026-11-08 before Offing ran on these additions.

Blind finding rule (2026-11-08): gh search code --limit 60 for each of extensions/v1beta1, batch/v1beta1, networking.k8s.io/v1beta1, and autoscaling/v2beta2 with --extension yaml; charts.helm.sh/stable with --filename Chart.yaml (Helm retired-repo pins); and extensions/v1beta1 with --filename kustomization.yaml (Kustomize overlays). Walk results in order; keep unique repositories that are not forks, not archived, not larger than 50,000 KB, and not already in the corpus; pin each at its default-branch HEAD that day.

Blind zero-finding rule (same day): GitHub repository search for small NetworkPolicy example repositories (kubernetes networkpolicy examples, stars 10..5000, not archived). Walk results in order; warm and scan offline; keep a repository only when every detector reports nothing; stop once the Kubernetes ecosystem has four empty expected lists. Kept zeros from that walk: fatihsoysalcom/kubernetes-network-policy-example and HaseebUllah-DevOps/kubernetes-security-policies (alongside the earlier targeted zeros).

Corpus-wide countEvidence for kubernetes meets every stable row. Offline validate on the Kubernetes bucket reported precision 1 and recall 1.

Java and Kotlin corpus

Twenty-five public repositories at pinned commits cover the java detector. Targeted (chosen knowing their result): kagkarlsson/db-scheduler (a multi-module Maven build, no findings), piomin/sample-spring-reactive (a java.version of 19), danvega/loom (java.version, source, and target of 19), krakowski/jextract-demo (a Gradle Kotlin DSL toolchain of 22), and Descended/Henesys (a mysql:mysql-connector-java 8.0.33 dependency, which the artifact's own POM relocates).

Blind (2026-10-23 rule below): jzyong/GameServer4j (JDK 13 and 14 compile levels across nine modules), latexdraw/latexdraw (java.version 14), amigoscode/login-registration-backend and TechPrimers/spring-batch-example-1 (java.version 15), moditect/jfrunit (java.version 16, plus actions/cache, actions/checkout, and actions/setup-java at v2), advanced-security/monorepo-filtering-workaround (java.version 18, plus actions/checkout@v3), ChristianAA/selenium-springboot-example (JDK 18, plus Action pins), stepstone-tech/doom-graalvm (java.version 19), vladannovi1234/ecommerce-springboot-react (JDK 19 compile levels in ten modules), and three with no Java finding: neo4j-examples/movies-java-spring-data-neo4j and stirante/RuneChanger (JDK 17 and 11, both LTS; the first also has SHA-pinned Action findings), and eh3rrera/graphql-java-spring-boot-example (JDK 11 in the project, JDK 16 only inside a Maven profile, which the detector does not judge).

Blind stable expansion (2026-11-07 rule below): maxithub/reactive-spring-tutorial and weltraumpirat/hexagonal_ddd (java.version 13), DomainDrivers/dd-java and LastBotInc/llama2j (java.version 20), mohamed-taman/Flight-Advisor and JPro-one/HelloJPro-Maven (java.version 22), mosh-hamedani/spring-store (java.version 23), and danvega/spring-boot-testing (JDK 21 LTS, empty expected).

Every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the Java ones, and each was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit. The ground truth is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of the repositories has a migration commit for the finding. The JDK dates come from the Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap and the Temurin support page, and the relocation from the Maven Central POM, not from these repositories. A run of npm run validate:public-repos -- --offline --ecosystem java on 2026-11-07 over the twenty-five Java entries reported no false positives or false negatives, with 70 expected java findings, all true (20 repositories with Java findings in the Java bucket; 4 zero-finding Java-ecosystem repositories; 20 of 25 blind). Corpus-wide countEvidence for java is 21 repositories with findings and 71 expected findings.

Java and Kotlin blind selection

The five earliest Java repositories were chosen knowing their result, so each records selection: "targeted"; the twelve below record selection: "blind".

The blind rule, fixed on 2026-10-23 before Offing ran on these additions: GitHub code search <java.version>N</java.version> restricted to filename:pom.xml, for N in 14, 15, 16, 18, 19 (non-LTS, expected to produce findings) and 17 (LTS, expected to produce none), gh search code --limit 60. Per N, walk the results in order and keep the first two unique repositories whose matching path is exactly the root pom.xml, skipping forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus, and repositories larger than 50,000 KB on GitHub. Pin each at its default-branch commit on that date. The twelve are, in order: jzyong/GameServer4j, latexdraw/latexdraw, amigoscode/login-registration-backend, TechPrimers/spring-batch-example-1, moditect/jfrunit, eh3rrera/graphql-java-spring-boot-example, advanced-security/monorepo-filtering-workaround, ChristianAA/selenium-springboot-example, stepstone-tech/doom-graalvm, vladannovi1234/ecommerce-springboot-react, neo4j-examples/movies-java-spring-data-neo4j, and stirante/RuneChanger. piomin/sample-spring-reactive was skipped (already pinned). The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list above, not a re-run, is the record.

Ground truth: for each repository every JDK declaration (java.version, maven.compiler.*, compiler-plugin source, target, and release, Gradle compatibility and toolchain settings, and .java-version, .sdkmanrc, .tool-versions) was listed with grep over the pinned files and compared with the report, independently of Offing's own output. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the Oracle roadmap fact the rule rests on.

Java and Kotlin stable expansion (2026-11-07)

To meet the stable evidence minimums of decision 0013 (21 repositories with Java findings, 4 zero-finding Java-ecosystem repositories, at least two thirds blind), the Java corpus gains further blind repositories. The selection rule below was fixed on 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on these additions.

Blind rule (2026-11-07): GitHub code search filename:pom.xml for <java.version>N</java.version> with N in 13, 20, 22, 23 (non-LTS, expected findings) and 21 (LTS, expected zero Java findings), gh search code --limit 60. Per N, walk the results in order; keep the first unique repositories whose matching path is exactly the root pom.xml; skip forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus, and repositories larger than 50,000 KB on GitHub. When pom search is exhausted for a version, also allow build.gradle.kts / build.gradle with JavaLanguageVersion.of(N) or sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_N / VERSION_N style. Pin each at its default-branch HEAD SHA on 2026-11-07. Prefer every new entry blind. Need enough new pins for seven repositories with Java findings and one zero-finding companion (JDK 21), so the bucket reaches 20 finding repositories and 4 zero-finding repositories.

The repositories kept by that walk, and the ground-truth notes for every finding on each pin (including other detectors), are recorded on the new benchmarks/public-repositories/java/ entries listed above.

Scala and sbt corpus

Eighty public repositories at pinned commits cover the scala detector. No public Scala corpus existed before 2026-11-07. The selection rules below were fixed on that date before Offing ran on any Scala addition. Scala 2.12 and 2.13 are intentionally not judged (still maintained); pins of those lines, and of Scala 3.3 LTS, are zero-finding / no-scala-finding controls. The corpus covers declaration forms .scala-version, build.sbt scalaVersion, and project/build.properties sbt.version. Rules in force: scala.runtime.eol-2.11, scala.runtime.eos-3.0-3.2, and scala.sbt.eol-0.13.

Blind alone reached stable evidence on 2026-11-07: 51 repositories with scala.* findings, 77 expected scala findings, 12 zero-finding Scala-ecosystem repositories, and all 80 repositories blind. No targeted multi-module additions were required. A run of npm run validate:public-repos -- --offline --ecosystem scala on that date reported precision 1 and recall 1 for scala.

Scala and sbt blind selection

Blind rule, fixed on 2026-11-07 before Offing ran: gh search code --limit 60 for each of:

  1. scalaVersion := "2.11 filename:build.sbt
  2. scalaVersion := "3.0 filename:build.sbt
  3. scalaVersion := "3.1 filename:build.sbt
  4. scalaVersion := "3.2 filename:build.sbt
  5. sbt.version=0.13 filename:build.properties
  6. 2.11. filename:.scala-version (content search for a 2.11 pin)
  7. Zero-finding queries: scalaVersion := "2.13, scalaVersion := "2.12, and scalaVersion := "3.3 filename:build.sbt

GitHub code search does not reliably match the := token, so the walk used equivalent quoted version strings in the same filenames ("2.11.12", "2.11.8", "2.11.11", "3.0.2", "3.1.3", "3.2.2", sbt.version=0.13.18 / 0.13.16, "2.13.12", "2.12.18", "3.3.3", and 2.11.12 in .scala-version) that still select repositories declaring those pins. Walk results in order; skip forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus, and repositories larger than 50,000 KB; keep when the default branch still has the matching file and the file still contains the pin. Pin each at its default-branch HEAD SHA on 2026-11-07. Need enough for stable counts (≥20 repositories with scala.* findings, ≥4 zero-finding Scala-ecosystem repositories, ≥⅔ blind, ≥60 scala.* expected findings). Prefer multi-module / nested project repositories for finding density. A few known multi-module finding-dense repositories may be added as targeted if blind alone cannot reach 60 findings; those are named as targeted in this section after selection.

Ground truth: for each pin every Scala/sbt declaration (and every other-detector finding on that pin) is read from the file and compared with the report. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the vendor lifecycle fact the rule rests on (Scala development guarantees, sbt download / support pages). The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list under benchmarks/public-repositories/scala/, not a re-run, is the record.

Ruby corpus

Sixty public repositories at pinned commits cover the ruby detector, 41 of them selected blind (68%) and 19 targeted. 39 have expected Ruby findings (229 in total); 37 have expected findings of any detector (378 in total) and 23 have none. The original five are rack/rack (no findings), Shopify/packwerk, thoughtbot/suspenders, github/view_component, and puma/puma (a Gemfile ruby "3.2.0" directive). The selection rule was fixed before the results were read: GitHub repositories whose language is Ruby, ordered by stars, taking those with a Gemfile or .ruby-version at the default branch head; targeted entries are added where a manual search of Gemfile and .ruby-version showed a declaration the sample otherwise missed (a multi-requirement ruby directive). Each entry's selection field records which rule applied

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the Ruby ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of these repositories has a reviewed migration entry in the mining log for the finding, so none is cited as migration-commit. The EOL dates come from the Ruby maintenance branches page, not from these repositories.

Each entry's selection field records which rule applied

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the PHP ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of these repositories has a reviewed migration entry in the mining log for the finding, so none is cited as migration-commit. Package abandonment comes from Packagist and the Laminas / Symfony announcements; the PHP 7.4 end-of-life date comes from the PHP unsupported branches page, not from these repositories.

Blind (rules below): the original seven from 2026-10-21, the later Swift corpus growth entries, and sixty-three repositories added on 2026-11-07 for the stable promotion. Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the Swift ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of these repositories has a reviewed migration entry in the mining log for the finding, so none is cited as migration-commit. Swift blind selection

The six earliest Swift repositories were chosen knowing their result, so each records selection: "targeted". Later entries record selection: "blind".

The first blind rule, fixed on 2026-10-21 before Offing ran on those additions: GitHub code search for filename:xcode-version. Walk unique repositories whose path is exactly .xcode-version, in the order returned that day. Skip a repository when it is a fork, archived, already in the corpus, not primarily Swift, or larger than 50,000 KB on GitHub. Keep it when the default branch still contains .xcode-version. Stop once the beta counts in decision 0013 are met, which happened at seven. The seven, pinned at their default-branch commit on that date, are search results 12, 19, 20, 22, 24, 28, and 31: paulgessinger/swift-paperless, microsoft/SwiftStreamingMarkdown, hhru/mvi-swift, babylonhealth/Stevenson, cgoldsby/TvOSMoreButton, micahflee/TM-SGNL-iOS, and griffin-stewie/BudouX.swift. Results before and between those were skipped by the rule above (size, language, or an existing pin), including signalapp/Signal-iOS, Simperium/simperium-ios, and seedco/Formalist. The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list above, not a re-run, is the record.

The stable-promotion blind rule, fixed on 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on the new additions: GitHub code search in this order — filename:.xcode-version (limit 100), IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 9 in filename:project.pbxproj (limit 60), then 14., 15., and 16.0 in filename:.xcode-version for older pins still on default branches. Walk each result list in order. Skip forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus, and repositories larger than 50,000 KB. Prefer Swift or Objective-C as the repository language for the Xcode-version queries. Pin each kept repository at its default-branch HEAD that day. Stop once the stable counts in decision 0013 are met with margin. The sixty-three new files under benchmarks/public-repositories/swift/ (indexes 0818–0880) are that batch. The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list, not a re-run, is the record.

Ground truth: for each repository the .xcode-version line, every application-target IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, and any other detector declaration on that pin were read from the file and compared with the report. Pins at Xcode 26 and later produce no Xcode finding under the bundled rules. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the vendor date the rule rests on.

Serverless corpus

Forty-one public repositories at pinned commits cover the serverless detector.

Targeted: Dwolla/webhook-receiver (provider.runtime nodejs14.x), haltakov/natural-language-image-search (provider.runtime python3.8), HUK-COBURG/innoforum-aws-serverless (SAM and Terraform nodejs14.x, plus GitHub Actions pins), BaptisteLecat/gcp_architect_certification (Terraform Google Cloud Functions nodejs14), and aws-samples/sam-python-crud-sample (five SAM python3.8 functions, plus GitHub Actions pins).

Blind (rule below): serverless/examples and AnomalyInnovations/serverless-stack-demo-api (no findings), Swizec/lambda-screenshot-as-a-service (nodejs14.x), skojin/send-gmail-lambda (ruby2.7), and livgust/covid-vaccine-scrapers (seven SAM nodejs14.x functions, plus Node.js and GitHub Actions pins).

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the Serverless ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line; none of these repositories has a reviewed migration entry in the mining log for the finding, so none is cited as migration-commit. The AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Functions end-of-life dates come from the AWS Lambda runtimes table and the Cloud Run functions runtime support schedule, not from these repositories.

Correction (new rules, 2026-10-31). Rules added after these entries were pinned now report on them, and the first corpus run listed each as unexpected: the Dockerfile legacy-env-format and maintainer rules on hasura/skor and kubernetes/examples, and the AWS Lambda rules for runtimes that are still supported (for example nodejs22.x, nodejs24.x, provided.al2) on serverless/examples, aws-samples/aws-lambda-extensions, serverlesspub/imagemagick-aws-lambda-2, and slackapi/bolt-js. Each was confirmed by reading the line at the pinned commit and added to expected with a maintainer-review note. That left hasura/skor and serverless/examples as no longer empty, so three targeted zero-finding entries were added to keep the beta evidence of decision 0013: kubernetes-up-and-running/examples (plain manifests), and BauplanLabs/quack-reduce and dvalbuena1/visa_rescheduler_aws (container-image and runtime-less Serverless Framework services, which declare no runtime for a rule to judge).

Serverless blind selection

The five earliest Serverless corpus repositories were chosen knowing their result, so each records selection: "targeted". The five below record selection: "blind".

The blind rule, fixed on 2026-10-21 before Offing ran on these additions: GitHub code search for runtime: nodejs14.x in filename:serverless.yml, plus the first results of Runtime: nodejs14.x / Runtime: python3.8 in SAM template.yaml and of current runtime: nodejs22.x examples, walking public non-fork repositories in the order returned that day. Keep a repository when its default-branch tip contains serverless.yml, template.yaml / template.yml, or a Terraform aws_lambda_function / google_cloudfunctions*_function runtime declaration; skip archives and the repositories already pinned as targeted. Stop at five. The five, pinned at their default-branch commit on that date, are serverless/examples, AnomalyInnovations/serverless-stack-demo-api, Swizec/lambda-screenshot-as-a-service, skojin/send-gmail-lambda, and livgust/covid-vaccine-scrapers. The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list above, not a re-run, is the record.

Ground truth: for each repository the runtime lines (and any other detector findings on the same pin) were listed by reading the pinned files and compared with the report, independently of Offing's own output. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the vendor date the rule rests on.

Serverless stable expansion (2026-11-08)

To meet the stable evidence minimums of decision 0013, the Serverless corpus gains further blind repositories. The selection rule below was fixed on 2026-11-08 before Offing ran on these additions.

Blind finding rule (2026-11-08): gh search code --limit 40 for nodejs14.x --filename serverless.yml, python3.8 --filename template.yaml, runtime = "nodejs14.x" --extension tf, and node_version = "14" --extension tf (Azure App Service / Functions pins). Walk results in order; keep unique non-fork, non-archived repositories under 50,000 KB that are not already in the corpus; pin each at its default-branch HEAD that day.

Blind zero-finding rule (same day): walk tiny image-oriented or empty-runtime candidates from repository search (serverless image packaging, small star counts); keep only when the offline scan reports nothing for every detector. Kept zeros: CloudNationHQ/terraform-azure-func (module with no literal stack pin) and api-evangelist/echo (alongside the earlier targeted zeros).

The same change wires Azure application_stack version pins to pkg:generic/azure-app-service/<stack> rules (regression fixtures under tests/fixtures/serverless/). Corpus-wide countEvidence for serverless meets every stable row. Offline validate on the Serverless bucket reported precision 1 and recall 1.

.NET blind selection

The six earliest .NET repositories were chosen knowing their result, so each records selection: "targeted". The selection field is optional on every corpus entry; "blind" means the repository was chosen by a rule fixed before Offing ran on it (decision 0013), and an entry without the field counts as not blind.

The blind rule, run on 2026-10-19: GitHub repository search for language:C#, 100 to 500 stars, last pushed from 2021-01-01 to 2024-12-31, not a fork, not archived, sorted by stars descending (gh search repos --language "C#" --stars "100..500" --updated "2021-01-01..2024-12-31" --archived=false --include-forks=false --sort stars --order desc). Walk the results in order and take each repository whose default branch has at least one *.csproj, *.fsproj, *.vbproj, or global.json; skip the others (Unity packages with no project file). Stop at twelve, whatever Offing reports for them. The twelve, pinned at their default-branch commit on that date, are results 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16 of that search: rikimaru0345/Ceras, takuya-takeuchi/DlibDotNet, 0xthirteen/SharpStay, NightfallGT/Mercurial-Grabber, Dec0ne/ShadowSpray, Ceiridge/Chrome-Developer-Mode-Extension-Warning-Patcher, TerribleDev/OwinOAuthProviders, chsakell/mvcarchitecture, SeriaWei/ASP.NET-MVC-CMS, stanzhai/Html2Article, BeichenDream/SharpToken, and nettitude/SharpSocks. Ranks 2, 4, 6, and 8 have no project file. The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list above, not a re-run, is the record.

Ground truth: for each repository the target frameworks, SDK pins, and package references were listed by grep over the pinned files and compared with the report, independently of Offing's own output. Every expected finding has a maintainer-review note naming the path, the exact line, and the vendor date the rule rests on. Ceras was the one miss: it targets netcoreapp2.1 and netcoreapp2.2, which had no rule, so the registry gained the 1.x, 2.x, and 3.0 lines in the same change.

CI runner images corpus

Five public repositories at pinned commits cover the ci-images detector: oatpp/oatpp (ubuntu-20.04 and ubuntu-22.04 hosted images), Chinachu/Mirakurun (four ubuntu-22.04 pools, plus a deprecated tslint dependency), microsoft/Sysmon-Linux (ubuntu-22.04, plus actions/checkout v4.1.1), aliostad/CacheCow (ubuntu-22.04, plus .NET target frameworks past or scheduled for end of support), and Windos/PoshNotify (Azure Pipelines pools that use only *-latest images, no findings).

Issue #1898 added 86 entries: 60 blind and 26 targeted. The first blind rule, fixed on 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on the results: GitHub code search for vmImage in files named azure-pipelines.yml, taking hits in the order returned, one repository once; skip forks, repositories already in the corpus, and repositories over 100,000 KB; take the first 35. They are: ardalis/GuardClauses, ardalis/SmartEnum, shahedc/NetLearnerApp, microsoft/SDCM, fastpack/fastpack, sestoft/C5, DigitalRuby/ExchangeSharp, imbushuo/EnergyStar, dotpcap/sharppcap, microsoft/vswhere, reanimate/reanimate, EducationalTestingService/skll, vkhorikov/CSharpFunctionalExtensions, danielga/garrysmod_common, Gericom/GBARunner2, microsoft/MSBuildSdks, ra1028/DiffableDataSources, seahorn/seahorn, gaelcolas/Sampler, microsoft/OpenXR-MixedReality, sixeyed/dockerfiles-windows, foonathan/array, alanmcgovern/Mono.Nat, analogdevicesinc/EVAL-ADICUP360, jet/FsKafka, UiPath/angular-components, ignatandrei/NETCoreBlockly, Amitpnk/Hexagonal-architecture-ASP.NET-Core, Azure/AppConfiguration-DotnetProvider, AugurProject/augur.js, sujiar37/AWX-HA-InstanceGroup, microsoft/MeshGraphormer, ivanpaulovich/FluentMediator, Simnico99/MicaWPF, and Foxlider/FASTER. That sample was almost all *-latest images, so a second blind rule was fixed the same day: the same search, restricted to repositories whose last push is between 2022-01-01 and 2023-12-31, first 25: zHaytam/SmartBreadcrumbs, vector-of-bool/pmm, dmyersturnbull/tyrannosaurus, Capgemini/xrm-datamigration, alexwang66/Guestbook-microservices-k8s, OfficeDev/microsoft-teams-apps-timetally, surge-synthesizer/tuning-workbench-synth, GoranHalvarsson/SitecoreBlazor, godsharp/GodSharp.Socket, dtylman/AWSRetriever, GriffinPlus/docker-strongswan, WinOpsDBA/DBAinTheCloud, StirlingLabs/Assimp.Net, shibayan/IISManager, hexawyz/NetUnicodeInfo, Softeq/mapbox-xamarin, ecampidoglio/Linker, CCRcmcpe/Auto-Arknights, tanathos/ClippyVS, psfinaki/CheckYourCzech, ZacBi/learn_NLP_again, kshitizadhikari/HexagonArchitecture1, attilaszasz/dotnet-catapult, sVathis/ebay-watchlist-calendar, and Sauceforge/SauceOpsMobile. The 26 targeted entries were chosen knowing they declare older images: GitHub code search for ubuntu-22.04 (14 repositories) and then ubuntu-20.04 (12) in azure-pipelines.yml, same skips, first hits in order. The searches return different results on another day, so the pinned list is the record. GitLab CI and CircleCI repositories are not added: the detector reads them but judges nothing, so they could not carry findings.

The ci-images corpus now has 98 entries, 67 blind (68%). 29 have expected CI image findings (63 in total) and 20 have no findings of any detector. A full offline run reported no false positives and no false negatives for the detector.

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding in these repositories is recorded, not only the CI image ones. Each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit, and its groundTruthSource is a maintainer-review note naming the path and line. The Azure dates come from the hosted image deprecation schedule and the Azure DevOps blog deprecation plan, not from these repositories. All five were chosen knowing their image labels, so each records selection: "targeted".

Container corpus

Issue #1898 added 30 container entries, all blind. The rule, fixed on 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on them: GitHub code search for FROM in files named Dockerfile, taking hits in the order the search returned them, one repository once. Skip forks, repositories already in the corpus, repositories over 100,000 KB, and repositories with more than 20 Dockerfile* files. Take the first 30. They are, in order: laradock/php-fpm, laradock/workspace, NVIDIA-Genomics-Research/AtacWorks, Haufe-Lexware/docker-style-guide, jcgay/maven-color, istepanov/docker-mongodump, dreasysnail/RetGen, aerospike/aerospike-dev-notebooks.docker, botchagalupe/DockerDo, logandk/serverless-rack, transferwise/wise-pizza, NSEcho/furlzz, s7anley/redis-sentinel-docker, onecompiler/cheatsheets, edyan/php-fpm, rootsongjc/cheatsheets, behance/docker-php, aerospike-examples/interactive-notebooks, dvmonroe/sanity-ruby, maidaly/Arabic_OCR, PremiereGlobal/freeswitch-docker, Comcast/Ravel, tedsluis/docker-dump1090, dramforever/os-lectures-build, estafette/estafette-extension-dotnet, upconsulting/IsisCB, chrishenry/deltanyc-heatseek, lucdotdev/youtube_tiktok, jbochi/bullock, and whorusq/learning-docker. The search skipped appleboy/golang-testing (27 Dockerfiles). The query returns different results on another day, so the pinned list, not a re-run, is the record.

The corpus now has 42 container entries, 37 blind (88%). Seven have no findings of any detector. A full offline run reported no false positives and no false negatives for the container detector.

Because the corpus scans every detector, every finding is recorded, not only the container ones, and each expected finding was checked by reading its line at the pinned commit.

Dart corpus

Issue #1894 promoted the dart detector to stable. The corpus holds 75 pinned Dart repositories: 55 selected blind (73%) and 20 targeted. Across the whole corpus the detector expects 138 findings in 31 repositories (30 of them in the Dart bucket, plus a Dart SDK pin in railwayapp/nixpacks); 18 Dart-bucket repositories have no expected findings of any detector.

Blind rule (fixed 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on these additions): GitHub repository search --language=Dart --stars='>=80' --archived=false, sorted by stars descending. Walk results in order; keep a repository when its default branch contains a pubspec.yaml, it is not a fork, it is not already in the corpus, and it is not a meta list such as awesome-flutter. Skip flutter/flutter (over the 100,000 KB size cap). Take the first 48. Pin each at its default-branch HEAD commit SHA on that day.

Targeted rule (fixed the same day): GitHub code search for >=2.17.0 <3.0.0 in filename:pubspec.yaml, taking hits in returned order, one repository once; skip forks, templates (.twig, .hbs, templates/), repositories already chosen, and repositories already in the corpus. Cap at 15. Earlier targeted entries cover exact SDK pins of Dart 3.8.

Ground truth: every finding in these repositories, from every detector, was read at its pinned line and recorded with a maintainer-review note naming the path and line. Dart end-of-support dates come from the Dart security policy and changelog.

Android corpus

Issue #1894 promoted the android detector to stable. The corpus holds 84 pinned Android repositories: 56 selected blind (67%) and 28 targeted. Across the whole corpus the detector expects 87 findings in 42 repositories (including Android findings declared in other ecosystems' pins); 22 Android-bucket repositories have no expected findings of any detector.

Blind rule (fixed 2026-11-07 before Offing ran on these additions): GitHub code search for targetSdk in filename:build.gradle, then the same for filename:build.gradle.kts. Walk hits in returned order, one repository once across both queries. Skip forks, archives, repositories already in the corpus, and paths that are not exactly build.gradle / build.gradle.kts or under a directory with those names. Take the first 48. Pin at default-branch HEAD.

Targeted rule (fixed the same day): GitHub code search for targetSdk 28 through targetSdk 30 in filename:build.gradle, and targetSdk = 33 / targetSdk = 34 in filename:build.gradle.kts, taking repositories whose matching path ends in build.gradle or build.gradle.kts. Skip forks, archives, already-chosen repositories, and template/backup suffixes. Cap so the blind share stays at or above two thirds.

Ground truth: every finding was read at its pinned line. Play Billing deprecation dates come from the Billing Library deprecation FAQ; the targetSdk floor comes from Google Play's target API level requirement.
